question: What would a TV ad campaign for Punctual Pros look like?
html:
A Punctual Pros TV campaign would be zip-targeted connected TV (CTV), not broadcast. It would sell the punctuality guarantees the three brands already make, and it would be judged on booked jobs against holdout zips (Punctual Pros ad plan, Oct 6, 2026).

Why streaming, not broadcast

  • Self-serve CTV now has $50-$500 minimums and roughly $15-40 CPMs with zip targeting (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • That lets a ~$22M franchisee buy TV in its ~240 zips. It avoids paying for the whole Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Candidate buying tools: Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads and YouTube on TV screens. Vibe quotes $15-35 CPMs and $50 per-strategy minimums (Punctual Pros ad plan).

Creative

  • No new claims. Each brand sells its existing promise (Punctual Pros ad plan):
  • One Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!"
  • Ben Franklin: $5-a-minute guarantee.
  • Mister Sparky: "America's On-Time Electrician."
  • There are two test cuts: "Storm Ready" (:15) and "We Watch the Clock" (:30, also cut to :15).
  • Delivery specs are 1920x1080, 16:9, at -24 LKFS ±2 dB loudness (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What TV is for

  • TV's job is to make the brand familiar before the furnace fails. It should also lift branded search and Local Services Ads conversion.
  • Local Services Ads stay the always-on base at $39-57 per lead (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Completion rate is not a success metric. It runs ~94-99% by construction.

Test sequence

WeekCTV action
1Tracking numbers, UTMs, pixels; hold out 15% of Tier-I zips
2Creative A/B, split 50/50 by zip cluster
3Check frequency (cap 3/week)
4Read booked jobs per 10k households vs holdout; shift 20% to winning cut
5Weather-triggered pacing in half the counties
6Vendor A/B: Vibe vs Disney Campaign Manager or YouTube

Source: Punctual Pros ad plan.

Gaps in the data

  • Weekly budgets of $8,000-$12,500 cover all channels, including mail and speed-to-lead tests. They are not CTV-only. The CTV share and a full-season total are not in the excerpt. The plan's line items would answer this.
  • The $12 cost per site visit is an assumption (est.) taken from consumer-brand case studies. No home-services CTV benchmark was found. It must be replaced by the week-8 read (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Cost per booked job from TV is unknown until holdout results arrive. Any figure before then is an est.

Next actions

  • Confirm the CTV share of weekly spend. Lock the Tier-I zip holdout list before launch.
  • Brief production on both cuts to the stated specs. Keep the copy to the existing brand guarantees.
  • Set up ServiceTitan tracking numbers and QR codes per creative. This lets week-4 reads tie to booked jobs.
  • Schedule the week-8 read to replace the $12 cost-per-visit assumption with actual data.
